chapter.name: Fundamental Rights
chapter.blurb: Articles 12 to 35: rights of equality, freedom, exploitation, religion, cultural and educational rights, property, constitutional remedies and the limits on Part III.

scope_in.item: Articles 27-28: tax for religion, religious instruction
Articles 29-30: cultural and educational rights; the right to property before and after 1978
Articles 31A, 31B, 31C and the Ninth Schedule; Article 32 and its comparison with Article 226
Articles 33-35, rights outside Part III, availability of rights, scheme of Part III

scope_out.item: Articles 12-26 (equality, freedoms, exploitation, freedom of religion)
scope_out.reason: covered by the sister pack aks05a

scope_out.item: Navy Act year, Article 28 'fourth category', 'agrarian purpose' limit of Article 31A, cooperative societies as 'corporation', Article 20 and 22 enemy-alien table row
scope_out.reason: notes disagree with the standard textbook or settled law; not tested

concepts.name: Articles 27-30: religious funding, instruction, cultural and educational rights, and the right to property
concepts.description: Tax for religion, religious instruction, minority rights and the old right to property.
concepts.idea: Articles 27-30 protect conscience, culture and minority institutions, and property moved out of Part III in 1978.
concepts.rule: Article 27 bars taxes, not fees, for promoting a religion. Article 28 bans religious instruction in wholly State-maintained institutions, exempts trust-based State-administered ones and requires consent in recognised or aided ones. Article 29 protects any section of citizens' culture and bars denial of admission on religion, race, caste or language; Article 30 gives minorities the right to run educational institutions, in three judicial types. Property was protected by Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 until the 44th Amendment (1978); Article 300A in Part XII remains.
concepts.example: A fee on pilgrims is valid, but a tax earmarked for one religion is not.

questions.q: A State government levies a fee on pilgrims at a shrine town to pay for sanitation and safety arrangements, and also spends part of its general tax revenue on policing a religious festival. Which of the following is correct under Article 27?
questions.a: The fee is outside Article 27, which bars a compulsory tax for promoting a religion and not a charge for a service
o: The fee is outside Article 27, which bars a compulsory tax for promoting a religion and not a charge for a service
The fee is invalid, because any compulsory levy collected at a place of worship amounts to a tax for promoting religion
The festival policing is invalid, because tax money may not be spent on any activity connected with a religious gathering
The fee is valid only if its proceeds are later returned to the pilgrims in the form of a refund
questions.e: Article 27 forbids compelling anyone to pay a tax whose proceeds are specifically used for a particular religion or denomination. It bars taxes, not fees; a fee is charged for a specific service. General State spending that only incidentally helps several religions is not barred.
w: A fee for a service is not a tax, and Article 27 prohibits only taxes.
General expenditure that incidentally benefits religions equally is not barred.
Nothing in Article 27 requires a refund; a fee is charged for a service rendered.

questions.q: Which one of the following institutions is exempted from the bar on religious instruction contained in Article 28(1)?
questions.a: An institution administered by the State but established under an endowment or trust that requires religious instruction
o: An institution administered by the State but established under an endowment or trust that requires religious instruction
An institution wholly maintained out of State funds, provided every student has given written consent
An institution recognised by the State, where attendance at the instruction is made compulsory for all students
An institution that receives aid from the State, provided the guardian of each minor has been informed in advance
questions.e: Article 28(2) exempts institutions administered by the State but set up under a trust or endowment that requires religious instruction. Article 28(1) is absolute for wholly State-maintained institutions, and Article 28(3) demands consent in recognised or aided ones.
w: Consent does not lift the absolute bar on wholly State-funded institutions.
In a recognised institution nobody can be required to attend religious instruction without consent.
Informing the guardian is not enough; consent is needed for a minor.

questions.q: Article 29(2) forbids denial of admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution on certain grounds. Which of the following is NOT one of the grounds named in that clause?
questions.e: Article 29(2) names religion, race, caste and language. Sex and place of birth appear in Article 15(1) but not in Article 29(2), so refusal on the ground of sex is attacked under Article 15.
w: Sex is named in Article 15(1), not in Article 29(2).
Caste is one of the four grounds of Article 29(2).
Race is one of the four grounds of Article 29(2).

questions.q: A minority-run college neither asks for recognition nor takes aid from the State. Which of the following best describes the State's power over it?
questions.a: It is bound only by general laws, such as those on contract, labour, taxation and crime, and runs its own administration
o: It is bound only by general laws, such as those on contract, labour, taxation and crime, and runs its own administration
It must follow the State's syllabus, teacher qualifications and academic standards, as an aided minority institution does
It is outside the reach of every law of the land, because Article 30 is an absolute right of minorities
It must obtain aid within three years, failing which its minority character lapses
questions.e: Judicially, minority institutions are of three types. Those seeking neither recognition nor aid have maximum autonomy, bound only by general laws (labour, tax, criminal, contract).
w: Control over syllabus and standards attaches to institutions seeking recognition or aid.
Article 30 is not absolute; general laws apply even to such an institution.
No such time limit exists; the third type is a recognised category in itself.

questions.q: Before the 44th Amendment, the Fundamental Right to property rested on two provisions. Which one of the following describes them correctly?
questions.a: Article 19(1)(f) gave citizens the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property; Article 31 protected every person against deprivation
o: Article 19(1)(f) gave citizens the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property; Article 31 protected every person against deprivation
Article 19(1)(f) protected every person including foreigners in acquiring property, while Article 31 was confined to citizens
Both Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 were confined to citizens, and non-citizens held property only under ordinary law
Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 both sat in Part IV and could be enforced only through the Directive Principles
questions.e: At the commencement of the Constitution, property was protected by Article 19(1)(f) for citizens and by Article 31 for all persons; this dual protection made it a strong Fundamental Right until the 44th Amendment.
w: It reverses the two provisions: 19(1)(f) was for citizens and Article 31 for all persons.
Article 31 covered citizens and non-citizens alike.
Both were in Part III as Fundamental Rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 27:

1. Article 27 prevents a person from being compelled to pay a tax whose proceeds are specially spent on promoting a particular religion or denomination.
2. A fee charged for a specific service, such as safety arrangements for pilgrims, is also prohibited by Article 27.
3. State expenditure on keeping order during religious festivals is barred by Article 27 because it benefits religious gatherings.
4. Article 27 guards against indirect coercion through taxation and so supports freedom of conscience.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; also. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 27 bars only taxes, not fees. Statement 3 is incorrect: General spending that only incidentally benefits several religions equally is not barred. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about religious instruction in educational institutions:

1. Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in an institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
2. A State-administered institution set up under a trust that requires religious instruction cannot give such instruction.
3. In a State-recognised or State-aided institution no person can be made to take part in religious worship without consent, or the guardian's consent in the case of a minor.
4. In Aruna Roy (2002) the Supreme Court held that Article 28(1) bars religious instruction but not education about religion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; also. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 28(2) exempts it from clause (1). Statement 3 is correct: Article 28(3). Statement 4 is correct.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 29:

1. Article 29(1) lets any section of citizens residing in India with a distinct language, script or culture conserve it.
2. Article 29(2) forbids denial of admission to a State-run or State-aided institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
3. In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) communal reservation in educational institutions was upheld under Article 29(2).
4. The Supreme Court held in D.A.V. College (1971) that State promotion of the majority language in itself violates Article 29(1).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Court struck it down, treating Article 29(2) as an enforceable individual right. Statement 4 is incorrect: It held that promoting Punjabi did not violate Article 29(1).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Article 29(2) with Article 15(1):

1. Article 29(2) is the wider clause because it applies to all State action, whereas Article 15(1) is confined to educational institutions.
2. Article 15(1) names sex and place of birth among its grounds, in addition to religion, race and caste.
3. Refusal of admission to a State-aided college on the ground of sex is a breach of Article 29(2).
4. Article 29(2) is a specific protection that applies to State-maintained or State-aided institutions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The reverse is true: Article 15(1) covers State action generally. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Sex is not a ground listed in Article 29(2); the breach is of Article 15. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:

1. Article 30(1) confers the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice on religious minorities only, not on linguistic minorities.
2. Under Article 30(2) the State cannot discriminate in granting aid against an institution managed by a religious or linguistic minority.
3. Article 30 also contains clause (1A), added by the 44th Amendment (1978), on compensation when a minority institution's property is compulsorily acquired.
4. Article 30 protects any section of citizens, minority or majority, that wishes to run an educational institution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It covers all minorities, religious or linguistic. Statement 2 is correct; also. Statement 3 is correct: Clause (1A) exists, so clauses (1) and (2) are not the whole of Article 30. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 30 applies only to minorities; Article 29 uses 'section of citizens'.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about minority educational institutions:

1. An institution seeking recognition and aid faces State control over curriculum, teacher qualifications and standards but must keep autonomy in administration.
2. Article 30 is meant to place minority institutions in a more advantageous position than institutions of the majority.
3. An institution seeking only recognition, and not aid, is subject to lesser control and has greater managerial freedom.
4. The State may deny aid to an institution merely because it is managed by a minority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; also. Statement 2 is incorrect: It gives equality, not privilege; there is no reverse discrimination. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: A minority institution cannot be denied aid for its minority status, and aid conditions must be neutral and uniform.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Property at the commencement of the Constitution:

1. Property was protected solely by Article 31, and Article 19(1)(f) did not deal with property at all.
2. Article 19(1)(f) gave citizens the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
3. Article 31 protected citizens and non-citizens alike against deprivation of property except by authority of law.
4. Compulsory acquisition under Article 31 required a public purpose and compensation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 19(1)(f) gave citizens the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct; also. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the present position of the right to property:

1. The dual protection of Article 19(1)(f) for citizens and Article 31 for all persons once secured the right to property within Part III.
2. Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 were taken out of Part III by the 44th Amendment (1978).
3. Article 300A, in Part XII, says that no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law.
4. After the repeal, property remains a legal or constitutional right but is no longer a Fundamental Right in Part III.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 19(1)(f) gave citizens and Article 31 gave all persons protection of property as Fundamental Rights in Part III. Statement 2 is correct: the 44th Amendment (1978) deleted both Articles from Part III. Statement 3 is correct: the same amendment inserted Article 300A in Part XII, so that no person is deprived of property save by authority of law. Statement 4 is correct: property is now a legal or constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: after the 44th Amendment property is a constitutional right under Article 300A, no longer a Fundamental Right.
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 once protected property within Part III.
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the 44th Amendment (1978) removed Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from Part III.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the term 'minority' and Articles 29-30:

1. The Jains were included in the first notification of national minorities issued after the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
2. The Constitution does not itself define the term 'minority'.
3. Article 29 is a protection of institutions while Article 30 is a protection of identity.
4. Article 30 is an individual right, whereas Article 29 is purely an institutional right.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Jains were added by a later notification (2014); the first list was shorter. Statement 2 is correct: The Constitution does not itself define the term 'minority'. Statement 3 is incorrect: The reverse: Article 29 protects identity, Article 30 institutions. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 29 carries individual plus collective rights; Article 30 is an institutional right.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about religious instruction and education about religion:

1. Religious instruction is doctrinal, sect-specific and ritual-oriented, while education about religion is academic, comparative and value-oriented.
2. State-administered institutions established under a trust may impart religious instruction.
3. In a State-aided institution religious instruction may be made compulsory for all students.
4. The Supreme Court held that comparative teaching of the values of all religions offends Article 28 and secularism.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Participation needs consent, or the guardian's consent for a minor. Statement 4 is incorrect: It held that such teaching does not offend Article 28 or secularism. So exactly 2 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 29 and 30:

1. Article 29 can be invoked by a section of citizens that forms a majority.
2. Article 30 applies only to minorities, religious or linguistic.
3. Article 29(1) is breached only when a minority's culture is stifled or extinguished.
4. Article 29(1) is breached whenever a minority culture is less widely practised than that of the majority.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; also. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: Mere difference in prominence is no breach. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble, Article 30 and the property provisions:

1. India was described as a 'secular' State in the Preamble from 1976, through the 42nd Amendment.
2. The article that now protects property was inserted into Part XII by the 42nd Amendment.
3. The Constitution itself defines the term 'minority' in Article 30.
4. Clause (1A) of Article 30 was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 300A was inserted by the 44th Amendment (1978). Statement 3 is incorrect: The term is not defined anywhere in the Constitution. Statement 4 is incorrect: It was added by the 44th Amendment (1978). So exactly 1 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements are correct (statements 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements are correct (statements 1).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the statements are correct (statements 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Religious instruction is prohibited in an institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
Statement-II: In a State-recognised or State-aided institution a minor cannot be required to take part in religious worship without the guardian's consent.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct (Article 28(1). Statement-II is correct (Article 28(3). Article 28(3) deals with a different kind of institution and does not explain the bar in clause (1).
w: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I: it concerns recognised or aided institutions, not wholly State-maintained ones.
Statement-II is not incorrect: Article 28(3) says exactly this.
Statement-I is not incorrect: Article 28(1) says this.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The protection of Article 29 is not confined to the notified minority communities.
Statement-II: Article 29 speaks of 'any section of citizens', a phrase wide enough to include a majority group.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Article 29(1) is not confined to notified minorities. Statement-II is correct, and II is the wording of the Article that causes I: 'any section of citizens' is wide enough to include a majority group.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I: the width of 'section of citizens' is why majorities are covered.
Statement-II is correct, so the option calling it incorrect fails.
Statement-I is correct, so the option calling it incorrect fails.

questions.q:
Match the decided case in List-I with the constitutional provision it concerned in List-II.

List-I (Case)
A. Aruna Roy v. Union of India (2002)
B. D.A.V. College, Jullundur v. State of Punjab (1971)
C. State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
D. Secretary of Malankara Syrian Catholic College (2006)

List-II (Provision)
1. Article 29(1)
2. Article 28(1)
3. Article 29(2)
4. Article 30(1)
questions.e: Aruna Roy challenged textbooks under Article 28(1). D.A.V. College concerned promotion of Punjabi and Article 29(1). Champakam struck down communal reservation, holding Article 29(2) enforceable. Malankara Syrian Catholic College (2006) summarised the Article 30(1) principles.
w: B and C are interchanged: D.A.V. concerned Article 29(1) and Champakam Article 29(2).
A and D are interchanged: Aruna Roy concerned Article 28(1) and Malankara Article 30(1).
A and B are interchanged: Aruna Roy concerned Article 28(1) and D.A.V. Article 29(1).

concepts.name: Articles 31A-31C and the constitutional remedy under Article 32
concepts.description: Exceptions to Fundamental Rights, the Ninth Schedule, Article 32 versus 226 and habeas corpus.
concepts.idea: Articles 31A-31C shield selected laws, bounded by the basic structure, while Article 32 guarantees the remedy.
concepts.rule: Article 31A saves five categories of laws from Articles 14 and 19; Article 31B protects the Ninth Schedule from all Fundamental Rights, subject to Coelho (2007) for laws after 24 April 1973; Article 31C covers laws for Article 39(b) and (c), the 42nd Amendment extension being struck down in Minerva Mills (1980). Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right with five writs, unlike the discretionary Article 226. Habeas corpus lies against public and private detention that is illegal.
concepts.example: A land reform law may escape Article 14 but not the basic structure.

questions.q: Article 31A saves certain categories of laws from being declared void for inconsistency with Articles 14 and 19. Which one of the following is NOT among those categories?
questions.a: Preventive detention of persons acting against public order
o: Preventive detention of persons acting against public order
Taking over the management of a property by the State for a limited period
Extinguishing or modifying rights arising from a mining lease or licence
Amalgamation of two or more corporations in the public interest
questions.e: Article 31A covers five categories: acquisition of estates and related rights, State takeover of management of property, amalgamation of corporations, extinguishment or modification of the rights of directors or shareholders, and of mining rights. Preventive detention is outside them.
w: Preventive detention is not one of the five categories of Article 31A.
This is category (b) of Article 31A(1).
This is category (e) of Article 31A(1).

questions.q: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after a certain date are open to judicial review. The cut-off date is the date of the judgment in
questions.e: Coelho held that all Ninth Schedule laws placed after 24 April 1973, the date of Kesavananda Bharati, are open to judicial review and cannot violate the basic structure.
w: Golak Nath is not the reference; the cut-off is the Kesavananda date, 24 April 1973.
Minerva Mills came later (1980) and is not the reference date.
Maneka Gandhi concerned Article 21, not the Ninth Schedule cut-off.

questions.q: Dr B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as
questions.a: the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it
o: the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it
the conscience of the Constitution, joining Parts III and IV
the Magna Carta of the Indian citizen
the keystone that fixes the federal balance
questions.e: Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul of the Constitution, since rights without remedies would be meaningless.
w: The 'conscience' description is used for the combination of Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, not by Ambedkar for Article 32.
'Magna Carta' is the label applied to Part III as a whole, not Ambedkar's phrase for Article 32.
Ambedkar spoke of remedies, not of federal balance.

questions.q: Article 32(4) says that the right guaranteed by Article 32 shall not be suspended
questions.a: except as otherwise provided by the Constitution itself
o: except as otherwise provided by the Constitution itself
except by an ordinary law of Parliament passed by a simple majority
except by Parliament through a law passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting
except by the President through an ordinance promulgated while Parliament is not in session
questions.e: Article 32(4): the right cannot be suspended except as the Constitution itself provides; the President's order during a national emergency under Article 359 is the instance of such a provision.
w: An ordinary law cannot suspend it; only the Constitution itself can provide for suspension.
Even a special majority law of Parliament cannot suspend it; the exception must come from the Constitution itself.
An ordinance is ordinary legislation; the President's power to suspend enforcement comes from Article 359 of the Constitution itself.

questions.q: In which one of the following situations can a writ of habeas corpus NOT be issued?
questions.a: A person is held in custody under the order of a competent court after trial
o: A person is held in custody under the order of a competent court after trial
A person is confined by a private individual without any legal authority
A detention order was passed in violation of a mandatory procedural safeguard
A person is detained by a public authority that has no legal power to detain
questions.e: Habeas corpus lies against public authorities and private persons where detention is illegal, lacks legal authority or violates mandatory safeguards; it is refused when detention is lawful, by a competent court, for contempt, or outside the court's jurisdiction.
w: Private confinement can be challenged by habeas corpus if illegality is proved.
Violation of mandatory procedural safeguards makes detention illegal and the writ lies.
Detention lacking legal authority is a ground for the writ.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the categories of laws saved by Article 31A:

1. Article 31A(1)(a) covers laws on the acquisition of estates or of rights in them.
2. Estates under Article 31A(1)(a) include land held under zamindari, jagirdari or similar tenures.
3. Article 31A(1)(b) protects laws under which the State takes over management of property permanently.
4. Article 31A(1)(c) protects laws that break up a corporation into several smaller corporations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: It covers takeover for a limited period, in public interest or for proper management. Statement 4 is incorrect: It protects laws amalgamating two or more corporations.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 31A:

1. Article 31A saves the covered laws from being declared void for inconsistency with Article 14 or Article 19.
2. Article 31A(1)(d) covers laws extinguishing or modifying the rights of managing agents, directors, managers or shareholders' voting rights.
3. Article 31A(1)(e) covers laws extinguishing or modifying rights under a mining lease or licence, including its premature termination.
4. Article 31A shields the covered laws against challenge under every Fundamental Right in Part III.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 31A saves the covered laws (acquisition of estates, management takeover, company and mining-lease laws) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19. Statement 2 is correct: Article 31A(1)(d) covers laws extinguishing or modifying the rights of managing agents, directors, managers or shareholders' voting rights. Statement 3 is correct: Article 31A(1)(e) covers rights under a mining lease or licence, including premature termination. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 31A shields against Articles 14 and 19 only; it is Article 31B that shields Ninth Schedule laws against all Fundamental Rights.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (Article 31A shields only against Articles 14 and 19) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: Article 31A(1)(e) covers mining leases and licences.
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Article 31A(1)(d) covers rights of managing agents, directors and shareholders.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule:

1. Article 31B provides that Acts and Regulations specified in the Ninth Schedule are not void on the ground of conflict with any Fundamental Right in Part III.
2. The immunity of Article 31B is wider than that of Article 31A, because Ninth Schedule laws are protected whatever their subject.
3. Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Ninth Schedule laws are immune even from a basic structure challenge.
4. Under I.R. Coelho (2007), all laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 31B protects Acts and Regulations in the Ninth Schedule from being void for conflict with any Fundamental Right. Statement 2 is correct: Article 31A covers only specified subjects, whereas Ninth Schedule laws are protected whatever their subject, so 31B is wider. Statement 3 is incorrect: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) did not give Ninth Schedule laws immunity from the basic structure; Articles 31A, 31B and 31C are limited by judicially evolved checks, chiefly the basic structure doctrine. Statement 4 is correct: in I.R. Coelho (2007) the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the basic structure doctrine limits Ninth Schedule laws) and leaves out statement 2, which is correct (Article 31B is wider than 31A).
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: Coelho (2007) opened post-1973 Ninth Schedule laws to judicial review.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 31B shields Ninth Schedule laws from Part III conflict.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 31B and 31C:

1. In Coelho the Court held that Ninth Schedule laws placed after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge for violating the basic structure.
2. Article 31C shields laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under every Fundamental Right in Part III.
3. For Article 31C, a bare declaration by the legislature that the law gives effect to Article 39(b) or (c) is enough to oust the Court's scrutiny.
4. Article 31C in its original form covered all the Directive Principles of Part IV.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: It shields only against Articles 14 and 19. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Court examines the substance of the law. Statement 4 is incorrect: It covered only Article 39(b) and (c); the 42nd Amendment extended it.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 31C and the decisions on it:

1. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the first part of Article 31C, giving immunity from Articles 14 and 19 to laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c), was upheld.
2. In Kesavananda Bharati the second part of Article 31C, which ousted judicial review, was also upheld.
3. The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 extended Article 31C to all Directive Principles in Part IV.
4. Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980) upheld that extension.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) upheld the first part of Article 31C (immunity from Articles 14 and 19 for laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c)). Statement 2 is incorrect: the second part, ousting judicial review, was struck down as violating the basic structure. Statement 3 is correct: the 42nd Amendment (1976) extended Article 31C to all Directive Principles. Statement 4 is incorrect: Minerva Mills (1980) held the extension unconstitutional.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (the judicial-review bar was struck down) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (Minerva Mills struck the extension down) and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: the 42nd Amendment extended Article 31C to all Directive Principles.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the present position of Articles 31A to 31C:

1. Minerva Mills held that the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is part of the basic structure.
2. Today Article 31C covers only laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c), and the basic structure doctrine applies to them.
3. The judicial limit on Article 31B laws is I.R. Coelho, and on Article 31C laws it is Minerva Mills.
4. Judicial review cannot be wholly excluded for laws protected by Article 31C.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Minerva Mills held that the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is part of the basic structure. Statement 2 is correct: Today Article 31C covers only laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c), and the basic structure doctrine applies to them. Statement 3 is correct: (comparison table). Statement 4 is correct: Judicial review cannot be wholly excluded for laws protected by Article 31C.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 32:

1. Article 32 is placed in Part III and is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. Article 32(2) empowers the Supreme Court to issue four writs, quo warranto being left to the High Courts.
3. Article 32(3) lets Parliament by law empower any other court to exercise, within its local limits, the Supreme Court's writ powers, without prejudice to the Supreme Court's own powers.
4. The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32(1) is discretionary, so the Court may decline to hear a petitioner.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 is in Part III and is itself a Fundamental Right (Dr Ambedkar called it the heart of the Constitution). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 32(2) empowers the Supreme Court to issue five writs, including quo warranto. Statement 3 is correct: Article 32(3) lets Parliament empower other courts to exercise these powers within their local limits. Statement 4 is incorrect: the remedy is guaranteed, not discretionary.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (the right to move the Court is guaranteed) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: Article 32(3) lets Parliament empower other courts.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (five writs, including quo warranto) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Article 32 and Article 226:

1. A petitioner can claim relief under Article 32 as of right, whereas relief under Article 226 rests in the High Court's discretion.
2. Article 32 can enforce Fundamental Rights as well as other legal rights.
3. The Supreme Court's writ power runs across India, whereas a High Court ordinarily acts within its territorial jurisdiction.
4. Article 32 operates through the Supreme Court and Article 226 through the High Courts, each issuing the written judicial orders known as writs.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: relief under Article 32 is a guaranteed Fundamental Right, whereas under Article 226 it rests in the High Court's discretion. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 32 enforces only Fundamental Rights; Article 226 also other legal rights. Statement 3 is correct: the Supreme Court's writ power runs across India; under Article 226(2) a High Court can also reach outside its territory where the cause of action arises within it. Statement 4 is correct: Article 32 operates through the Supreme Court and Article 226 through the High Courts, each issuing the written judicial orders known as writs.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (Article 32 enforces only Fundamental Rights) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 32 relief is a right, Article 226 relief is discretionary.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: Article 32 does not cover ordinary legal rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about writs and habeas corpus:

1. Under Article 32 the High Courts, and under Article 226 the Supreme Court, are empowered to issue directions, orders or writs.
2. Habeas corpus literally means 'to have the body' and protects personal liberty against illegal detention.
3. A petition for habeas corpus can be filed only by the detained person himself.
4. The writ is issued when detention is illegal, lacks legal authority or violates mandatory procedural safeguards.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The pairing is reversed: Article 32 for the Supreme Court, Article 226 for the High Courts. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: A third party acting bona fide may file, and strict locus standi rules do not apply. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the right to constitutional remedies:

1. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the heart and soul of the Constitution.
2. The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 cannot be suspended except as the Constitution provides.
3. The President can suspend the right to move any court for enforcing Fundamental Rights during a national emergency under Article 359.
4. Parliament may suspend Article 32 by an ordinary law whenever it considers it necessary.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: Only the Constitution itself can provide for suspension. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of habeas corpus:

1. A bona fide third party may seek the writ on behalf of the detained person.
2. The writ lies against private individuals too, if illegal confinement is proved.
3. The writ is available even when the proceeding is for contempt of a court or legislature.
4. The writ is not available against private individuals at all.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: a bona fide third party may seek habeas corpus for the detained person. Statement 2 is correct: the writ lies against private individuals too, if illegal confinement is proved. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is not issued where the detention is under a proceeding for contempt of a court or legislature. Statement 4 is incorrect: it lies against private persons too. So exactly 2 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Rights and the Ninth Schedule:

1. Article 31A(1)(c) protects laws splitting a corporation into two or more corporations.
2. In the comparison table, Article 31B shields against Articles 14 and 19 only.
3. In Coelho the Court gave blanket immunity from review to Ninth Schedule laws.
4. Habeas corpus is barred against private persons.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It protects laws amalgamating corporations. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 31B shields against all Fundamental Rights. Statement 3 is incorrect: It held that such laws cannot violate the basic structure. Statement 4 is incorrect: It lies against both public authorities and private persons. So exactly 0 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 0 of the statements are correct (statements none).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 0 of the statements are correct (statements none).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 0 of the statements are correct (statements none).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The widened scope given to Article 31C in 1976 is no longer good law.
Statement-II: Minerva Mills (1980) held that the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is part of the basic structure.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the extension was held unconstitutional. Statement-II is correct: and gives the reason: giving all Directive Principles primacy would upset the balance that forms part of the basic structure.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I: the balance doctrine is the ground on which the extension fell.
Statement-II is correct, so the option that rejects it fails.
Statement-I is correct, so the option that rejects it fails.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A High Court may refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction under Article 226.
Statement-II: Article 226 lets a High Court enforce ordinary legal rights as well as Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 32 enforces only Fundamental Rights.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the High Court's power under Article 226 is discretionary, so it may refuse to exercise it. Statement-II is correct: Article 226 covers ordinary legal rights as well as Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 32 covers only Fundamental Rights. Both are correct; II concerns the scope of rights covered, not the discretion to refuse, so it does not explain I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is true but does not give the reason for Statement-I. II concerns the scope of rights covered, not the discretion to refuse, so it does not explain I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, not incorrect. Article 226 covers ordinary legal rights as well, while Article 32 covers only Fundamental Rights.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, not incorrect. A High Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is discretionary.

questions.q:
Match the constitutional provision in List-I with the matter it covers in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 31A
B. Article 31B
C. Article 31C
D. Article 32(2)

List-II
1. Laws giving effect to Article 39(b) and (c)
2. Laws on acquisition of estates and mining rights
3. Acts and Regulations placed in the Ninth Schedule
4. Power of the Supreme Court to issue five kinds of writs
questions.e: Article 31A covers estates, management, amalgamation, directors and mining rights; Article 31B the Ninth Schedule; Article 31C laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c); Article 32(2) the five writs.
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 31A is about estates and Article 31B about the Ninth Schedule.
B and C are interchanged: Article 31B is about the Ninth Schedule and Article 31C about Article 39(b) and (c).
C and D are interchanged: Article 31C is about Article 39(b) and (c) and Article 32(2) about the writs.

concepts.name: The writs, Articles 33-35 and the availability of Fundamental Rights
concepts.description: Mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto, armed forces, martial law and who may claim which right.
concepts.idea: Each writ has its own target, ground and exceptions, and Parliament alone shapes rights for the forces and martial law.
concepts.rule: Mandamus commands a public duty and is not issued against the President or Governors; prohibition forbids a lower body before its final order and certiorari quashes after it; quo warranto tests title to a substantive public office. Article 33 lets Parliament restrict rights of the armed forces and similar forces; Article 34 allows indemnity and validation under martial law; Article 35 gives Parliament exclusive law-making on certain rights. Articles 15, 16, 19 are for citizens, Articles 14, 21, 25, 32 for all persons.
concepts.example: A writ of prohibition is sought before the order; certiorari after it.

questions.q: The writ of mandamus cannot be issued against
o: a corporation performing a public duty
a local authority that has failed to act
an inferior tribunal in respect of its administrative acts
questions.e: Mandamus lies against the Union or State government, public officials, statutory bodies, local authorities, corporations with public duties and inferior tribunals (administrative acts); it cannot be issued against the President, State Governors or private individuals.
w: Mandamus can issue against corporations performing public duties.
Local authorities are among the bodies against which mandamus lies.
Inferior courts or tribunals are covered for administrative, not judicial, acts.

questions.q: A tribunal has already passed a final order that it had no jurisdiction to pass. Which writ is the appropriate remedy to have that order quashed?
questions.e: Prohibition stops proceedings before the final order; certiorari quashes the order after it is passed, on grounds such as lack of jurisdiction.
w: Prohibition is issued before the final order to stop the proceedings; here the order is already passed.
Mandamus commands performance of a public duty and does not quash an order.
Quo warranto tests a claim to public office, not a tribunal's order.

questions.q: The writ of quo warranto can be used to challenge a person's holding of
questions.a: a substantive public office of permanent character created by statute or the Constitution
o: a substantive public office of permanent character created by statute or the Constitution
a private office created by a trust deed for managing a family estate or a religious endowment
a ministerial post of a subordinate kind filled by a purely discretionary appointment
a contractual post that the holder occupies for a fixed term under an agreement
questions.e: Quo warranto ('by what authority?') lies only against the holder of a substantive public office created by statute or the Constitution; it is not issued for private, ministerial or contractual posts.
w: Private offices are outside quo warranto.
Ministerial offices are outside quo warranto.
Contractual or temporary posts are outside quo warranto.

questions.q: Which authority is empowered by Article 33 to decide, by law, how far the Fundamental Rights apply to members of the armed forces?
questions.a: Parliament, and not the State legislatures
o: Parliament, and not the State legislatures
The President, by an order issued under Article 359
The State legislatures, for the police forces of their own States
The Supreme Court, by issuing guidelines to the services
questions.e: Article 33 lets Parliament, by law, restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of the armed forces, forces for public order and intelligence bodies; State legislatures have no such power.
w: Article 33 gives the power to Parliament by law, not to the President by order.
The power is conferred only on Parliament.
The Court does not frame such restrictions; Parliament does by law.

questions.q: Article 34 deals with Fundamental Rights while martial law is in force in an area. Under it, Parliament is empowered to
questions.a: indemnify any person for acts done to maintain or restore order in the area
o: indemnify any person for acts done to maintain or restore order in the area
declare martial law in any part of India on the advice of the Council of Ministers
suspend the right to life and personal liberty throughout the country
extend the term of the Lok Sabha during the period of martial law
questions.e: Article 34 empowers Parliament to indemnify Union or State servants or any other person for acts done to maintain or restore order, and to validate sentences, punishments or forfeitures under martial law.
w: Article 34 does not itself declare martial law; the power is implicit, and it confers an indemnity power.
Article 21 is not suspendable; Article 34 does not suspend it.
Extending the Lok Sabha's term is a feature of national emergency, not martial law.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writs of mandamus and prohibition:

1. Mandamus literally means 'we command'.
2. Mandamus can issue against an inferior court or tribunal, as well as a public official, to perform a duty it has failed or refused to perform.
3. Mandamus will lie to enforce a contractual obligation of a public body.
4. Prohibition is available against an administrative body acting on its own discretion in matters of policy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Mandamus literally means 'we command'. Statement 2 is correct: Mandamus can issue against an inferior court or tribunal, as well as a public official, to perform a duty it has failed or refused to perform. Statement 3 is incorrect: It will not lie to enforce contractual obligations. Statement 4 is incorrect: Prohibition is not issued against administrative authorities.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of prohibition:

1. Prohibition literally means 'to forbid'.
2. It lies against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities exercising adjudicatory powers.
3. Its grounds include lack of jurisdiction, excess of jurisdiction, violation of natural justice and action under an unconstitutional statute.
4. It is not issued when the authority is acting within its jurisdiction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mandamus and prohibition:

1. Mandamus cannot be issued to enforce a departmental instruction that has no statutory force.
2. Mandamus can be issued against a State Governor but not against the President.
3. Prohibition is available against private individuals and bodies if they usurp adjudicatory functions.
4. Mandamus can be issued against a corporation performing public duties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: mandamus cannot enforce a departmental instruction that has no statutory force. Statement 2 is incorrect: it cannot be issued against either the President or State Governors. Statement 3 is incorrect: prohibition is not issued against private individuals or bodies; it lies only against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities. Statement 4 is correct: mandamus can be issued against a corporation performing public duties.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (mandamus does not lie against Governors either) and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: prohibition does not lie against private bodies.
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: mandamus cannot enforce a non-statutory departmental instruction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of certiorari:

1. Certiorari literally means 'to be certified' or 'to be informed'.
2. A mere error of fact is enough ground for certiorari.
3. Its grounds include error of law apparent on the face of the record and violation of natural justice such as bias.
4. Certiorari is not issued against legislative bodies or private individuals.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: A mere error of fact is not enough; the error must be of law apparent on the face of the record. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scope of certiorari:

1. Certiorari lies against tribunals and statutory bodies exercising adjudicatory powers.
2. The Supreme Court later ruled that certiorari can also issue against administrative authorities affecting the rights of individuals.
3. Certiorari is refused when an equally effective alternative remedy exists.
4. Certiorari is available against proceedings that are purely administrative and involve no adjudication.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct: the Supreme Court later ruled that certiorari can also issue against administrative authorities affecting the rights of individuals. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is refused for such proceedings.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ of quo warranto:

1. Quo warranto literally means 'by what authority?'.
2. It lies against the holder of a substantive public office created by the Constitution or a statute.
3. It can be issued where an office not created by any law is public in nature.
4. It is not issued for ministerial or contractual posts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The office must be created by the Constitution or a statute. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quo warranto, certiorari and prohibition:

1. Prohibition directs activity, while mandamus directs inactivity.
2. Any interested person may file a quo warranto petition, and the petitioner need not be personally aggrieved.
3. Quo warranto can be issued against the holder of a temporary or contractual post if the appointment is unlawful.
4. Certiorari is refused where the only error is one of fact.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Mandamus directs activity and prohibition directs inactivity. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is not issued when the post is temporary or contractual. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 33 and 34:

1. Article 33 also covers persons employed in bureaus or organisations set up by the State for intelligence purposes.
2. 'Members of the armed forces' in Article 33 is limited to combatants and excludes cooks, clerks and mechanics.
3. The Army Act, 1950 is a law made under Article 34 to regulate martial law.
4. Article 34 empowers a State legislature to validate any sentence passed or punishment inflicted under martial law in the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 33 also covers persons employed in bureaus or organisations set up by the State for intelligence purposes. Statement 2 is incorrect: It includes support staff such as cooks, clerks, barbers and drivers. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Army Act, 1950 is a law made under Article 33 for the armed forces. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 34 lets Parliament, not a State legislature, validate such acts.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the availability of Fundamental Rights:

1. Articles 15 and 16 are available only to citizens.
2. Article 19 can be claimed by foreigners residing in India.
3. Articles 25 and 32 are available to citizens and foreigners alike.
4. Articles 14 and 21 are not available to foreigners.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 19 is available only to citizens. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: They are available to citizens and foreigners alike, except enemy aliens.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 35 and rights outside Part III:

1. Article 265, in Part XII, says that no tax can be levied or collected except by authority of law.
2. Article 301, in Part XIII, guarantees freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India.
3. Article 300A is located in Part XIII.
4. Article 35 vests in Parliament, and not in the State legislatures, power to make laws on certain Fundamental Rights matters, to secure uniformity across India.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 265 in Part XII provides that no tax is levied or collected except by authority of law. Statement 2 is correct: Article 301 in Part XIII guarantees freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 300A is in Part XII. Statement 4 is correct: Article 35 vests in Parliament alone the power to make laws on certain Fundamental Rights matters, for uniformity across India. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scheme and history of Part III:

1. Part III originally had seven rights and now has six.
2. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
3. In Gopalan (1950) the Court required the procedure under Article 21 to be fair, just and reasonable, while Maneka Gandhi (1978) took a narrow view.
4. The Right to Constitutional Remedies is spread over Articles 32 to 35.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The two are reversed: Gopalan took the narrow view, Maneka Gandhi required fair procedure. Statement 4 is incorrect: The right to constitutional remedies is Article 32 alone. So exactly 2 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the armed forces, martial law and citizenship-based rights:

1. Article 34 deals with Fundamental Rights while martial law is in force in an area.
2. Article 29, protecting the language, script and culture of any section of citizens, is among the rights available to citizens only.
3. Article 33 enables Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces, so as to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline.
4. A law under Article 33 may be made by a State legislature for the police force of its own State.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 34 restricts Fundamental Rights while martial law is in force. Statement 2 is correct: Article 29(1) speaks of 'any section of the citizens', so it is available to citizens only. Statement 3 is correct: Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of the armed forces to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and discipline. Statement 4 is incorrect: only Parliament has this power, not a State legislature. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the statements are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: statement 4 is incorrect because Article 33 vests the power in Parliament alone.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A writ of prohibition cannot be obtained after a tribunal has delivered its final order.
Statement-II: Certiorari is the writ that stops a tribunal's pending proceedings, and prohibition is the writ that quashes its final order.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: prohibition stops proceedings before the final order, so after it the remedy is certiorari. Statement-II reverses the timing and is incorrect.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is incorrect, so the option accepting both fails.
Statement-I is correct, so the option rejecting it fails.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A law of Parliament can restrict the right of a mess cook of the armed forces to form an association.
Statement-II: The expression 'members of the armed forces' in Article 33 is not limited to combatants.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict such rights. Statement-II is correct: and is the reason a non-combatant cook is covered.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I: a cook is covered precisely because the term includes non-combatants.
Statement-II is correct (cooks, clerks, barbers are included), so rejecting it fails.
Statement-I is correct, so rejecting it fails.

questions.q:
Match the situation in List-I with the writ that fits it in List-II.

List-I (Situation)
A. A municipal officer refuses to perform a duty cast on him by a statute
B. A quasi-judicial body is about to hear a case outside its jurisdiction
C. A person's occupation of a statutory public office is challenged as without legal title
D. A person is confined by an authority with no legal power to detain him

List-II (Writ)
1. Prohibition
2. Quo warranto
3. Mandamus
4. Habeas corpus
questions.e: Mandamus commands a public official to do a duty; prohibition forbids a lower body from exceeding jurisdiction; quo warranto asks 'by what authority' a public office is held; habeas corpus 'to have the body' tests detention.
w: A and B are interchanged: a statutory duty calls for mandamus and an impending excess of jurisdiction for prohibition.
C and D are interchanged: title to office is tested by quo warranto and illegal confinement by habeas corpus.
B and C are interchanged: excess of jurisdiction needs prohibition and title to office quo warranto.
